title: UPDATE: Google Cloud Scales to 960,000 Nvidia GPUs to Cut AI Clusters to Single Node

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Ineffable Intelligence, the venture founded by AlphaGo creator David Silver, has become the first customer to access NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems on Google Cloud's new A5X instances. These instances will become generally available to all customers next month and are slated for expansion into Europe. Google will scale this infrastructure across multiple data center sites to support up to 960,000 Rubin GPUs, using ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, Virgo networking, and fourth-generation liquid cooling to optimize reinforcement learning and large-scale AI training.

Early tests by advertising group WPP showed that AI agent workloads utilizing NVIDIA Nemotron and OpenShell, which previously required a multi-node cluster, can run on a single A5X instance. Google is also making Confidential Computing generally available on G4 VMs with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs, with future plans for A4X Max instances powered by GB300 NVL72. To manage power constraints, the companies are deploying NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS technology to increase deployment density while maintaining existing data center power limits.

GOOGLE CLOUD & NVIDIA PLAN TO SCALE VERA RUBIN INFRASTRUCTURE TO UP TO 960,000 GPUS

Google Cloud announced that its new A5X instances, powered by NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, will become generally available next month, with plans to expand availability to Europe.

The new infrastructure is designed to support large-scale AI training, inference, autonomous AI agents, and reinforcement learning.

Here's what was announced:

• 960,000 Rubin GPUs: Google Cloud plans to scale its Vera Rubin infrastructure to as many as 960,000 GPUs across multiple data center sites.

• A5X Instances: Combine NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72, ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, Google Cloud's Virgo networking, and fourth-generation liquid cooling to support demanding AI workloads.

• Ineffable Intelligence: The company founded by AlphaGo creator David Silver became the first customer to access A5X, using it to develop "superlearners" that continuously improve through experience.

• WPP: Tested AI-powered creative workflows using NVIDIA Nemotron and OpenShell on A5X. Initial tests showed that workloads previously requiring a multi-node cluster could run on a single A5X instance.

• Confidential Computing: Google Cloud is also expanding secure AI infrastructure, making Confidential Computing generally available on G4 VMs powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs, with plans to bring rack-scale capabilities to GB300 NVL72-powered A4X Max instances.

Google Cloud and NVIDIA are also exploring new power-efficiency technologies through NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS to support larger AI deployments within existing data center power limits.

selectedTweets.text:
Google Cloud will open its Vera Rubin-based A5X instances to all customers next month.

In early tests by London advertising group WPP, AI agent workloads that previously needed a cluster of several servers ran on a single A5X instance.

Outside each rack, ConnectX-9 network cards and Google’s Virgo network tie racks together, letting Google Cloud scale the setup to 960K Rubin GPUs across multiple sites.

The design targets reinforcement learning, where models repeatedly generate experience, score results and retrain, so faster CPU-to-GPU and GPU-to-GPU links shorten each round.
